newsitem.title: UK: Natwest leads sector lower amid rate worries.
newsitem.headline: Natwest leads sector lower amid rate worries.

text.p: Shares in Natwest led others in the UK bank sector lower amid perceptions interest rates are headed higher still, dealers said.
The Bank of England raised its minimum lending rate by a quarter point to six percent on October 30 but governor Eddie George warned again today that further rises might be needed.
By 1056 GMT, Natwest shares had dipped 7p to 6641-1/2p, the lowest level since late September. Shares in Barclays Plc sank 8-1/2p to 938p, while shares in Abbey National fell 3p to 645p.
Abbey National shares fell under the additional weight of a sell note from Kleinwort Benson, they said. The shares previously had been restricted.
The sector slipped on today's economic figures which showed a 0.5 percent increase in UK producer input prices in October, fuelled by a sharp rise in oil prices.
"There are still rate worries out there and there will be a lot more concern if Thursday's (October retail price) figures are poor," said one marketmaker.
